---
title: "Developing with AI coding agents"
---

This article is for developers who work on rdborrow with an AI coding agent
such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Gemini CLI. The repository tells
agents how the package is built, so the agent's first draft follows the
package's conventions. Your job shifts to stating the task precisely and
checking the result.

## How agents learn the package's conventions

`AGENTS.md`, at the top of the repository, is a plain markdown file of
instructions that most coding agents read automatically. Claude Code reads
`.claude/CLAUDE.md` instead, which imports `AGENTS.md`, so every agent
follows the same rules from a single file. `AGENTS.md` is listed in
`.Rbuildignore`, so it never ships with the package.

It covers:

| Section | What the agent learns |
|---|---|
| Architecture | The user-facing API, the method class hierarchy, how `estimate()` dispatch works, and the `_core()` / `_se()` / `_boot_statistic()` pattern |
| Key commands | How to run tests, re-document, build the site, and run `R CMD check` |
| Coding | Base R only, base pipe, R 4.1 compatibility, checkmate validation, comment style |
| Testing | Where tests go, which expectations to use, and that a bug fix needs a failing test first |
| Documentation and `NEWS.md` | When to add roxygen docs, pkgdown entries, and NEWS bullets |
| Specialized tasks | Where to find the tidyverse instructions for argument checking and deprecation |
| Before committing | The one-line validation command to run before every commit |

For Claude Code, `.claude/settings.json` also pre-approves routine commands
such as `Rscript`, `grep`, and `gh issue view`, so the agent doesn't stop to
ask before running tests.

## A workflow that works

1. **Start from an issue.** An issue gives the agent a fixed statement of the
   problem and gives the PR something to close.
2. **Ask for a plan before code.** Reading a plan takes a minute; unwinding a
   wrong approach takes much longer.
3. **Write the test first.** Have the agent write a test that fails for the
   right reason, and confirm it fails, before it touches the fix.
4. **Let the agent implement and validate.** `AGENTS.md` tells it to run
   styler, re-document, and run the before-committing check.
5. **Review the diff yourself.** Read every changed line, starting with the
   statistics.
6. **Open a PR that references the issue.**

## Example prompts

### Add a method

[Adding a new method](adding-a-method.html) is written so that an agent can
follow it step by step. Give the agent the estimator's definition and point it
at the article:

```text
Add a new primary-analysis estimator to rdborrow called ec_or(), an
outcome-regression estimator for external control borrowing as defined in
<paper, equation number>.

Follow vignettes/articles/adding-a-method.Rmd step by step and use
R/ec_ipw.R as the template. Before writing the estimator, write
tests/testthat/test-full_pipeline_ec_or.R against reference values that I
will provide, and confirm that it fails. Then implement the method until
the test passes and devtools::check() is clean.
```

### Fix a bug from an issue

```text
Read issue #86 with `gh issue view 86 --comments`. Write a test that
reproduces the bug and confirm that it fails. Then fix the bug, add a
NEWS.md bullet, and run the before-committing check.
```

### Deprecate an argument

```text
Deprecate the <argument> argument of <function>(), following the
deprecation instructions referenced in AGENTS.md. Update the tests and
NEWS.md.
```

## Checking the agent's work

An agent can produce a clean, passing, well-documented change that is
statistically wrong. These habits catch that:

- **Supply the reference values yourself.** Take them from the paper, the
  authors' code, or a hand calculation. An agent that writes both the
  estimator and its expected output can encode the same mistake in both.
- **Review the math line by line.** For an estimator, that is
  `.{name}_core()` and `.{name}_se()`; the rest is plumbing.
- **Keep changes additive.** A new estimator only adds files. If the diff
  touches `run_analysis()`, an existing method, or a shared helper, ask why.
- **Treat a changed regression test as a red flag.** The
  `test-full_pipeline_*.R` files lock every method's output on
  `SyntheticData`. A changed number needs an explanation in the PR.
- **Run the full check.** `devtools::test()` uses `load_all()`, which can
  hide problems that only appear in the installed package.
  `devtools::check()` doesn't.

## Keeping `AGENTS.md` current

`AGENTS.md` is the single source of the package's conventions for both
people and agents. When a convention changes, update `AGENTS.md` in the same
PR. Add new rules there, not to `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so that every agent
sees them.
